source.title: Scaling Behaviors of LLM Reinforcement Learning Post-Training: An Empirical Study in Mathematical Reasoning
source.authors: Ze-Lin Tan; He-Jia Geng; Xiaohan Yu; Mu-Lei Zhang; Guan-Cheng Wan; Yi-Fan Zhou; Qiang He; Xiangyuan Xue; Heng Zhou; Yu-Tao Fan; Zhong-Zhi Li; Zai-Bin Zhang; Guibin Zhang; C. Zhang; Zhen-Fei Yin; P. Torr; Lei Bai

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some figure content is flattened, but the paper's accompanying descriptions are available.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law analysis to LLM reinforcement-learning post-training for mathematical reasoning, a training regime distinct from pretraining.
record.gate_note: The paper's metric is test loss defined as 1 − (correct solutions / total), not held-out cross-entropy. It tests scaling and prediction for RL post-training and reports downstream-task transfer. The discussion of pretraining scaling laws in related work is background, not evidence from this study.
record.test_reason: The study fits a power-law (log-linear) relation between RL post-training test loss (1 − pass rate) and compute or data across Qwen2.5 (0.5B–72B) and Llama 3 (1B–70B). It tests it by extrapolating from smaller models and from early training steps. This bears on V5, the same power-law form in another training regime, and partly on V7 (fit-dependence and bending curves). It has no pretraining cross-entropy results, so V1–V4 and V6, as stated for pretraining, are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that RL post-training test loss is log-linear (power-law) in compute and data. Fits on smaller models or early steps predict larger-model efficiency and late trajectories. Learning efficiency k(N) saturates with model size. Moderate data reuse is effective in data-constrained regimes. A Llama 3 check shows the form is architecture-agnostic. They caveat that absolute coefficients depend on task/benchmark and the result is limited to math, ≤72B and dense models.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines RL post-training with GRPO and pass-rate-derived test loss, rather than pretraining cross-entropy scaling and compute-optimal allocation experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Fitted Kmax and N0 differ across intra- versus inter-model fitting, model family, and compute versus data dimensions (Table 6). The authors also state that absolute coefficients depend on benchmark/task construction and difficulty. Data-reuse outcomes differ at τ = 100.

fits_no_version.finding: Under equal RL compute, Qwen2.5-32B initially beats 72B because it takes more steps, a model-size/steps trade-off.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RL post-training under a fixed compute budget, the loss-minimising model size is not always the largest available.

fits_no_version.finding: RL learning-efficiency coefficient k(N) rises with model size but saturates beyond about 32B (Kmax about 0.13–0.16 for Qwen).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The RL post-training scaling exponent grows with base model size and saturates.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed total data, final RL test loss is insensitive to reuse factor τ ≤ 25 and overfits at τ=100 (7B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In RL post-training, moderately repeated data is nearly as good as unique data.

fits_no_version.finding: Math RL improves other math benchmarks, leaves HumanEval/SuperGPQA flat, and degrades Zebra Puzzle for the largest models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling RL post-training compute transfers within domain but not out of domain.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2025)
record.problems: The primary metric is pass-rate-derived test loss, not cross-entropy. Experiments are limited to mathematical RL post-training, principally GRPO and dense Qwen2.5/Llama 3 families; the authors note no verification beyond 72B and no MoE generalization test. Many curve values appear only in figures. The paper reports three repeats and standard deviations/SEMs in Table 5, but no uncertainty for the prediction curves.
record.rows_left_out: No separately tabulated rows for every plotted model-size point or each downstream benchmark curve; figures provide many such values without corresponding numerical text. The reported aggregate scaling/prediction findings and explicit downstream-task statements are retained.

untested.parts: All as stated: no extrapolation of pretraining loss across orders of magnitude. RL extrapolation spans only 32B→72B.
All: no fitted compute-optimal parameter/token allocation exponents.
All: no shape/architecture ablation at fixed parameter count.
Image/video modalities and supervised fine-tuning. RL beyond mathematics, models beyond 72B, MoE models, and RL algorithms other than GRPO. Whether a power-law form holds under repeated data.
All: downstream performance as a function of pretraining scale or pretraining loss.
Parameter counting, schedule and data choices in pretraining; direct Kaplan vs Hoffmann comparison.

missing.what: Final held-out test loss per model size with SDs/SEMs (e.g. Qwen Base 0.9419 at 0.5B to 0.4359 at 72B; Llama Instruct 0.9446 at 1B to 0.5499 at 70B).
Alternative loss-decomposition model fits on the first 30% of steps (R2 0.995; D0 and λ per size), and 72B extrapolation with two calibrated parameters.
GRPO rollout size G ablation: optimal G shifts with compute budget, showing the curves depend on an algorithm hyperparameter.

record.verdict_notes: The loss is 1 − pass rate under GRPO post-training of already pretrained models, not pretraining cross-entropy. Only V5 (other training regimes) and, loosely, V7 are bearing versions. 'Inter-model prediction' predicts the slope k(N) for a 72B model about 2x larger than the fit range, so it is weak evidence for extrapolation across orders of magnitude. No quantitative prediction error is reported; fit quality is given only as R2.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of held-out cross-entropy loss for much larger pretraining runs; the tested setting is RL post-training test loss, with extrapolation from up to 32B to 72B.
The study compares models under compute budgets, but does not estimate power-law growth exponents for the compute-optimal parameter and token allocations.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No image/video modality or fine-tuning/transfer regimes beyond mathematical-reasoning RL post-training and the reported data-reuse setting.
The study evaluates transfer from math RL post-training, not downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss.
The study does not test every possible parameter-counting, schedule, data, or fitting-method choice, nor directly compare the Kaplan and Hoffmann pretraining laws.

rows.operation_detail: Fit compute and data scaling relationships across the Llama 3 model series.
rows.measure: Fit of compute- and data-loss scaling relationships
rows.value: R2 > 0.99 for both dimensions; Llama-70B peaks at approximately 50% holdout accuracy versus Qwen-72B at approximately 59%.
rows.note: Test loss is 1 − pass rate; this is an RL post-training result, not pretraining cross-entropy.
rows.check: Drop V2. This is a fit-quality result (R2 > 0.99), not an extrapolation test. The accuracy comparison (Llama-70B about 50% vs Qwen-72B about 59%) is context, not a scaling result.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 Base and Instruct models
rows.operation_detail: Compare test loss under equivalent compute budgets across model sizes.
rows.value: The 32B model outperforms the 72B model initially; the paper attributes this to the smaller model enabling more training steps.
rows.note: The paper describes a performance crossover; it does not report a fitted compute-optimal parameter/token allocation law.
rows.check: V3 concerns compute-optimal parameter/token allocation in pretraining. Here pretrained checkpoints are RL-tuned and no allocation exponent is fitted. The 32B-beats-72B crossover is a different construct; move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 models
rows.operation_detail: Fit learning-efficiency coefficient as a function of model size.
rows.value: Efficiency increases with model size, with gains diminishing beyond 32B; the fitted form approaches a saturation limit.
rows.note: This is RL post-training test-loss behavior, not a pretraining cross-entropy result.
rows.check: Saturation of the RL learning-efficiency coefficient k(N) with model size is not a quantity named by any version; move to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 and Llama 3 model families
rows.operation_detail: Compare fitted compute/data scaling coefficients across families and intra-/inter-model fitting protocols.

conditions.value: Qwen2.5 Base, Qwen2.5 Instruct, Llama 3 Instruct

rows.value: Table 6 reports different Kmax and N0 values across fitting protocols, model families, and resource dimensions; all reported R2 values exceed 0.99.
rows.note: For example, Qwen2.5 Base compute Kmax is 0.135 intra and 0.152 inter; N0 is 13.1B and 17.4B, respectively.
rows.check: This is the RL post-training regime, not the pretraining laws V7 primarily refers to. Kmax and N0 shift with intra vs inter fitting: Qwen Instruct L(N,C) N0 is 17.3B vs 28.3B; Llama Kmax is 0.089 vs 0.074.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5 models
rows.operation_detail: Fit an alternative loss-decomposition model and examine local log-log slopes.
rows.measure: Shape of loss curve and effective local slope
rows.baseline: single power-law approximation in the main formulation
rows.value: The appendix describes an S-shaped transition in log-log coordinates; the effective slope vanishes at low- and high-data limits and peaks around D ≈ D0(N).
rows.note: This is presented as an alternative formulation fitting the same dataset, not as a rejection of the main model's useful approximation.
rows.check: The appendix says learning curves are S-shaped in log-log coordinates, so the local slope varies. A single power law is only an approximation of the dominant trend; this qualifies V5 and supports V7's 'curves bend away'.

source_check.correct: V5 state: partial. V7 state: observed. The alternative model has a data-dependent local exponent that vanishes at both data limits; this qualifies V5 and directly exhibits V7.

source_check.problem: The shared partial state fits V5 but not V7, for which curvature away from a single power law is the claimed effect.
